<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919889_theRebbe_263" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919889_theRebbe_263__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Introductory heading "B'Siyata Dishmaya".</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the verse "Vehayah ekev tishma'un" and its connection to thought, speech, and action, culminating in the revelation of Atzmus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And it shall be, because you will hearken... and you will guard and you will do them..."</t>
    <t s="1">And the precise point in this is known,</t>
    <t s="2">for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos depends on man's choice,</t>
    <t s="3">and it should have said "And it shall be, if you will hearken"</t>
    <t s="4">[like "If</t>
    <t s="5">you walk in My statutes,</t>
    <t s="6">and it shall be</t>
    <t s="7">if you surely hearken"],</t>
    <t s="8">so why does it say "And it shall be, because you will hearken"?</t>
    <t s="9">For the meaning of the language is that you will surely hearken.</t>
    <t s="10">And the Tzemach Tzedek explains</t>
    <t s="11">that "ekev" refers to the time of the heels of Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="12">and this is "And it shall be, because you will hearken" —</t>
    <t s="13">you will surely hearken,</t>
    <t s="14">for the Torah promised that ultimately Israel will repent at the end of their exile, and immediately they will be redeemed.</t>
    <t s="15">And he continues in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="16">that the three expressions,</t>
    <t s="17">"you will hearken," "you will guard," and "you will do,"</t>
    <t s="18">are thought, speech, and action.</t>
    <t s="19">"You will hearken" is thought,</t>
    <t s="20">for the essence of hearing is in thought</t>
    <t s="21">(and the ear is merely a vessel through which sound enters his thought),</t>
    <t s="22">and "you will guard" is speech,</t>
    <t s="23">for the essence of guarding is with the mouth, as it is said,</t>
    <t s="24">"arranged in all and guarded,"</t>
    <t s="25">and "you will do" is action.</t>
    <t s="26">And upon this it continues and says,</t>
    <t s="27">"And Hashem your G-d will guard for you the covenant and the kindness which He swore..."</t>
    <t s="28">Covenant, kindness, and oath are thought, speech, and action</t>
    <t s="29">(as explained there at length),</t>
    <t s="30">and through "you will hearken," "you will guard," and "you will do,"</t>
    <t s="31">the service of thought, speech, and action of man,</t>
    <t s="32">there are drawn to him the thought, speech, and action from above,</t>
    <t s="33">"the covenant and the kindness which He swore."</t>
    <t s="34">However,</t>
    <t s="35">this matter</t>
    <t s="36">(that the thought, speech, and action from above should be drawn to man)</t>
    <t s="37">is still insufficient,</t>
    <t s="38">for even before the soul's descent below, it was in the most supernal level of this,</t>
    <t s="39">the thought above —</t>
    <t s="40">"Israel arose in thought,"</t>
    <t s="41">and the descent of the soul below is for the sake of an ascent,</t>
    <t s="42">so that through its service below it will ascend to a level more elevated than it was before the descent,</t>
    <t s="43">even to the level of "And You</t>
    <t s="44">guard it within me"</t>
    <t s="45">(which is above even the level of "pure"</t>
    <t s="46">it is).</t>
    <t s="47">And this is what is said, "And He will guard... the covenant and the kindness which He swore...",</t>
    <t s="48">that through "because you will hearken," "you will guard," and "you will do,"</t>
    <t s="49">the service of thought, speech, and action in the "heel" of the soul, which refers to the soul within the body,</t>
    <t s="50">and particularly in the heels of Moshiach</t>
    <t s="51">[an addition in the descent,</t>
    <t s="52">and consequently,</t>
    <t s="53">also in the ascent that comes through the descent],</t>
    <t s="54">that through the descent into a body and animal soul</t>
    <t s="55">(and particularly in exile),</t>
    <t s="56">the service of thought, speech, and action of the soul is with will and desire and in a manner of self-sacrifice</t>
    <t s="57">(above comprehension),</t>
    <t s="58">through this there will be "And He will guard... the covenant and the kindness which He swore..."</t>
    <t s="59">(specifically "guard"),</t>
    <t s="60">that the thought, speech, and action from above will have within them the revelation of "And You guard it within me,"</t>
    <t s="61">which in general is the matter of</t>
    <t s="62">the revelation of the Awtsmoos.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the Tzemach Tzedek's interpretation of "ekev" to the Midrash on reward, linking the service of self-sacrifice in the heels of Moshiach to the future revelation of Atzmus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">b)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, the above explanation</t>
    <t s="2">(of the Tzemach Tzedek)</t>
    <t s="3">regarding "And it shall be, because you will hearken"</t>
    <t s="4">(that "ekev" is an expression of end and refers to the end of days)</t>
    <t s="5">can be connected with the statement of the Midrash</t>
    <t s="6">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="7">The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them... their reward</t>
    <t s="8">(the reward of the mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="9">"in the heel" I give to you...</t>
    <t s="10">(as it is said)</t>
    <t s="11">"And it shall be, because you will hearken."</t>
    <t s="12">However, according to the Midrash which speaks of the reward of mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="13">the intent of "ekev"</t>
    <t s="14">(the end of days)</t>
    <t s="15">is for the time after the coming of Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="16">and according to the simple understanding of the matter which speaks of the fulfillment of mitzvos</t>
    <t s="17">("you will hearken... and you will guard and you will do them"),</t>
    <t s="18">the intent of "ekev"</t>
    <t s="19">(the end of days)</t>
    <t s="20">is for the end of the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="21">the heels of Moshiach.</t>
    <t s="22">And the connection between the two explanations is,</t>
    <t s="23">for the reward of mitzvos that will be "in the heel"</t>
    <t s="24">(in the future to come)</t>
    <t s="25">is that then there will be the revelation of the Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="26">as explained in Tanya.</t>
    <t s="27">And since this revelation is through the service</t>
    <t s="28">(of Torah and mitzvos in a manner)</t>
    <t s="29">of self-sacrifice</t>
    <t s="30">(as above),</t>
    <t s="31">therefore,</t>
    <t s="32">through "because you will hearken" according to the Tzemach Tzedek's explanation,</t>
    <t s="33">the service in the heels of Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="34">when self-sacrifice is greatest,</t>
    <t s="35">through this there will be the revelation of the future to come,</t>
    <t s="36">"in the heel I give to you."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
